sections.h2: Selling in Pompano Beach: your options
sections.html:
Pompano Beach is a beach city in the north of Broward County, halfway between Miami and Palm Beach. Year-round residents number over 101,400, and the count passes 150,000 when part-time owners come back for winter.

That seasonal pulse shapes a sale. Showings pick up while snowbirds are in town, and an empty house can sit quietly through summer. A seller with postponed repairs, a tenant or a lien on the house generally has three ways to go.

  • Hire an agent: expect repair requests, open houses and a closing date that follows the buyer's lender.
  • Sell directly to a neighbor or relative, in which case you handle the price and the paperwork.
  • Take a cash offer for the house as it stands, with you choosing the closing day.

Owners and renters make up close to equal shares. You will find older single-family blocks, mid-century duplexes and newer condos and townhomes side by side, so one citywide price says little about a particular address. Sellers range from retirees to heirs to landlords, and their needs differ.

Think about how the house will be used. Investors may buy to rent it out, while owner-occupants often want a move-in-ready place. A cash buyer will price in the repairs, whereas a retail buyer may ask you to make them. Knowing who your likely buyer is helps you pick the right route.

Homes near the Pompano Beach Air Park may hear aircraft, and the city publishes quiet-flying guidelines because of the effect on residential areas. If your street is affected, mention it early.

sections.h2: Flood zones and insurance near the water
sections.html:
A house near the water brings questions about flood zones and insurance. Before a buyer asks, collect your policy, any elevation certificate, and permits for roof, window or seawall work. One folder with all of it speeds the buyer's review and firms up a cash offer.

The oceanfront draws buyers to the 1,000-foot fishing pier, the redeveloped beachside fishing village and the early-1900s Hillsboro Lighthouse near the inlet. Inland blocks sell on price and commute, so describe what is special about your own street.

sections.h2: What the Broward homestead exemption means when you sell
sections.html:
If taxes are unpaid when you sell, the closing agent pays them out of your proceeds so the buyer receives a clean record. Ask the Broward tax collector for the balance in writing before the closing date, and ask whether any special assessment sits on the parcel.

Your exemption stops when you sell. It does not run past the year of the sale, and the next occupant must apply on their own.

Applications are due March 1 each year, with September 20, 2027 as the last possible late-filing date for the 2027 year. Renting the house out would likely cost you the exemption, and a change you fail to report can lead to back taxes, a 50 percent penalty and 15 percent interest.

After ownership changes, Florida re-values the property, which is why a buyer's first bill often exceeds yours. Sales, foreclosures and title transfers all trigger the reset, though transfers between spouses are an exception.

  • Hold on to the annual receipt Broward mails in January.
  • End the exemption on any house you no longer live in.
  • Ask about portability if your next Florida homestead starts within three tax years.

It may affect what buyers are willing to pay. Amendment 3 passed on November 3, 2026. It raises the non-school homestead exemption to as much as $150,000 for 2027 and $250,000 for 2028, and it lowers the non-homestead cap to 5 percent.

Implementing legislation will settle some details, so ask Broward's property appraiser how the changes will reach your parcel.

sections.h2: Costs and paperwork for a Pompano Beach deed
sections.html:
On a deed, Florida charges 70 cents per $100 of consideration everywhere except Miami-Dade. All parties to the document are liable, so the purchase contract should settle who pays.

The Broward clerk records the deed and takes the tax at that time. Under section 28.24, recording starts at $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each page after, before technology surcharges. Ask for a quote.

  • Obtain payoff statements from each mortgage and lien holder.
  • Have the closing agent prorate the Broward tax bill.
  • Check city permit and code records for open items.
  • Arrange two witnesses for the signing, which Florida requires for land conveyances.

sections.h2: What if the house has tenants, a foreclosure case or an heir?
sections.html:
Each situation can lead to a sale, but each has its own clock. For a tenant, ending a month-to-month tenancy takes 30 days' notice (section 83.57), and unpaid rent begins with a three-day written notice (section 83.56).

In a foreclosure, the clerk's sale is set 20 to 35 days after final judgment unless it is extended (section 45.031). Closing before then protects your equity.

Heirs can use summary administration when the estate is $150,000 or less, or when the death was more than two years ago (section 735.201).

Timing matters in a city with a busy winter season. Houses tend to draw more attention when seasonal owners are in town, so if you are in no rush, listing in that stretch may bring more showings. If you need to move sooner, a cash offer lets you set the date regardless of the calendar.

  1. Tell the buyer the address, mortgage balance and any tenant details.
  2. Review the written offer for price, repairs and closing day.
  3. The closing agent searches title and requests payoff letters.
  4. Two witnesses watch you sign the deed.
  5. The Broward clerk records it, and you receive your proceeds.

Before you talk to anyone, assemble a short packet: your payoff statement, the latest Broward tax bill, any lease, your insurance declarations page and the permits you have on file for major work. Ask each buyer how long the offer stays open and who pays for the title policy. Written answers protect you if the closing day moves.

On signing day, expect to review the settlement statement line by line. It should show the stamp tax, recording fees, payoffs and the prorated tax bill. If a line differs from your contract, ask the closing agent to correct it before you sign. Once the clerk records the deed, funds are released and the sale is final.

Cash removes the buyer's appraisal and loan approval, the two steps that most often stretch a listing. Title work and signing stay. Afterward, file your recorded deed, settlement statement and tax records together.

faqs.q: Is a cash offer quicker than an agent listing here?
faqs.a: Usually, because no lender appraisal is needed. The title still has to be clear, and the deed must be witnessed and recorded in Broward.

faqs.q: Who covers the deed stamps on a Pompano Beach sale?
faqs.a: Your contract decides, though the state can hold every party liable. Outside Miami-Dade the rate is 70 cents per $100.

faqs.q: Will my homestead exemption pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. It ends with the sale year, and the buyer must apply again before March 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell while I am behind on the mortgage?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as you close before the clerk's foreclosure sale. Act early, because that sale can fall 20 to 35 days after judgment.
